1	// Program Buffer execution helpers for the RISC-V Debug Module.
2	//
3	// Follows the same duck-typed template pattern as dmi_poll.hpp so that
4	// resume_driver.hpp can include this header without a circular dependency.
5	// Bus type requirement: write(uint8_t reg, uint32_t val) and
6	//                       read(uint8_t reg) -> uint32_t.
7	//
8	// Debug Spec references: section 3.6 (Program Buffer), table 3.1 (DMI),
9	// section 3.7.1.3 (Abstract Command - Access Register).
10	
11	#pragma once
12	
13	#include "hybrid/abstract_command.hpp"
14	#include "hybrid/dmi_poll.hpp"
15	
16	#include <array>
17	#include <cstdint>
18	#include <span>
19	#include <stdexcept>
20	#include <string>
21	
22	namespace hybrid {
23	
24	// DMI address of the first Program Buffer register (progbuf0..progbuf15).
25	inline constexpr uint8_t kProgbuf0 = 0x20u;
26	
27	// Max payload instructions: 16 total slots minus 1 reserved for the
28	// mandatory ebreak that terminates execution.
29	inline constexpr std::size_t kProgbufMaxInsns = 15u;
30	
31	// Standard ebreak encoding (funct12=1, opcode=SYSTEM).
32	inline constexpr uint32_t kEbreak = 0x00100073u;
33	
34	// "Execute Program Buffer only" command (Debug Spec table 3.1):
35	//   cmdtype  = 0 (Access Register)
36	//   aarsize  = Bits64 (3) - ignored by DM when transfer=0, set for consistency
37	//   postexec = 1 (bit 18)
38	//   transfer = 0 (bit 17 NOT set) - skip register I/O, only run progbuf
39	//   write    = 0 (irrelevant when transfer=0)
40	//   regno    = 0 (irrelevant when transfer=0)
41	inline constexpr uint32_t kExecProgbufCmd =
42	    (uint32_t(AarSize::Bits64) & 0x7u) << 20 | (1u << 18);
43	
44	// Encode `vsetvl rd, rs1, rs2` (RVV 1.0 section 6.2, funct7=1000000).
45	// Tier-B restore: stage vl in rs1 and vtype in rs2 via Abstract Commands,
46	// then branch-free-restore both in one Program Buffer execution.
47	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vsetvl(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, uint8_t rs2)
48	{
49	    return (0b1000000u << 25)
50	         | ((uint32_t(rs2) & 0x1Fu) << 20)
51	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
52	         | (0b111u << 12)
53	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
54	         | 0x57u;  // OP-V opcode
55	}
56	
57	// Encode `csrrw rd, csr, rs1` (SYSTEM opcode, funct3=001).
58	// Tier-A PB fallback: stage the CSR value in rs1 via Abstract Command,
59	// then write it to a CSR that the DM cannot reach via abstract access.
60	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_csrrw(uint8_t rd, uint16_t csr, uint8_t rs1)
61	{
62	    return ((uint32_t(csr) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
63	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
64	         | (0b001u << 12)
65	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
66	         | 0x73u;  // SYSTEM opcode
67	}
68	
69	// Encode `vle8.v vd, (rs1)` - unit-stride vector load, EEW=8 (RVV 1.0 sec 7.4).
70	// Fields: vm=1 (unmasked, bit 25), width=000, mop=00, mew=0, nf=000,
71	// lumop=00000, opcode LOAD-FP=0x07. PB V-regfile reload sweeps v0..v31 from
72	// the shared scratch region after a vsetvl to e8/m1.
73	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vle8_v(uint8_t vd, uint8_t rs1)
74	{
75	    return (1u << 25)
76	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
77	         | ((uint32_t(vd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
78	         | 0x07u;  // LOAD-FP opcode
79	}
80	
81	// Encode `vse8.v vs3, (rs1)` - unit-stride vector store, EEW=8. Mirror of
82	// encode_vle8_v with opcode STORE-FP=0x27. PB V-regfile dump sweeps v0..v31
83	// back to the shared scratch region at drain.
84	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vse8_v(uint8_t vs3, uint8_t rs1)
85	{
86	    return (1u << 25)
87	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
88	         | ((uint32_t(vs3) & 0x1Fu) << 7)
89	         | 0x27u;  // STORE-FP opcode
90	}
91	
92	// Encode `addi rd, rs1, imm12` (OP-IMM opcode 0x13, funct3=000). The batched
93	// V-data sweep advances the scratch base pointer x7 by one register-span
94	// between transfers WITHIN a Program-Buffer execution, so the per-register
95	// abstract x7 write disappears. imm12 is a signed 12-bit field (-2048..2047).
96	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_addi(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
97	{
98	    return ((uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
99	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
100	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
101	         | 0x13u;  // OP-IMM opcode (funct3=000)
102	}
103	
104	// Write insns[0..n-1] to progbuf0..n-1 and kEbreak to progbuf[n].
105	// Clears any sticky abstractcs.cmderr (W1C), issues kExecProgbufCmd, polls
106	// until abstractcs.busy clears, then verifies cmderr stayed clear.
107	//
108	// Throws std::runtime_error if insns.size() > kProgbufMaxInsns, if the poll
109	// times out, or if the DM raises cmderr during execution. No caller has a
110	// legitimate reason to silently continue on PB failure - the hart state
111	// would be partially restored / partially drained, which is worse than
112	// surfacing the fault.
113	template<typename Bus>
114	inline void exec_progbuf(Bus& bus, std::span<const uint32_t> insns)
115	{
116	    if (insns.size() > kProgbufMaxInsns)
117	        throw std::runtime_error(
118	            "exec_progbuf: too many instructions ("
119	            + std::to_string(insns.size()) + " > "
120	            + std::to_string(kProgbufMaxInsns) + ")");
121	
122	    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < insns.size(); ++i)
123	        bus.write(static_cast<uint8_t>(kProgbuf0 + i), insns[i]);
124	    bus.write(static_cast<uint8_t>(kProgbuf0 + insns.size()), kEbreak);
125	
126	    if ((bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) & kAbstractcsCmderrMask) != 0u)
127	        bus.write(kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsCmderrMask);
128	
129	    bus.write(kDmiCommand, kExecProgbufCmd);
130	    poll_until_clear(bus, kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsBusy, "exec_progbuf busy");
131	
132	    const uint32_t cmderr = bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) & kAbstractcsCmderrMask;
133	    if (cmderr != 0u)
134	        throw std::runtime_error(
135	            "exec_progbuf: PB execution raised cmderr="
136	            + std::to_string(cmderr >> 8));
137	}
138	
139	// vtype encoding for e8, m1, ta, ma (vsew=000, vlmul=000, vta=1, vma=1).
140	// The V-data sweep loads/stores one byte-element per lane (vl=vlenb).
141	inline constexpr uint32_t kVtypeE8M1 = 0xC0u;
142	
143	// Abstract-command write of a 64-bit value to Debug Module register `regno`
144	// (GPR/CSR/FPR): DATA0/DATA1 + Access-Register(write) + busy-poll. Free
145	// function so ResumeDriver, StateDrain, and the V-data sweep share one copy.
146	template<typename Bus>
147	inline void write_register_abstract(Bus& bus, uint16_t regno, uint64_t value)
148	{
149	    bus.write(kDmiData0, static_cast<uint32_t>(value & 0xffffffffu));
150	    bus.write(kDmiData1, static_cast<uint32_t>((value >> 32) & 0xffffffffu));
151	    bus.write(kDmiCommand,
152	              access_register_command(regno, AarSize::Bits64, /*write=*/true));
153	    poll_until_clear(bus, kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsBusy,
154	                     "write_register_abstract");
155	}
156	
157	// Sweep all 32 V data registers between the hart regfile and a contiguous
158	// scratch region via the Program Buffer. load=true issues vle8.v
159	// (scratch -> regfile, on resume); load=false issues vse8.v (regfile ->
160	// scratch, at drain). The leading vsetvl to e8/m1 sets vl=vlenb (one
161	// byte-element per lane) and forces vstart=0, so each unit-stride access
162	// covers the whole register even when the hart had vstart!=0. Uses x5/x6
163	// (vsetvl operands) and x7 (base pointer) as scratch. `stride` is the
164	// per-register byte spacing in the scratch region (the wire format reserves
165	// HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX per reg, independent of the runtime vlenb).
166	template<typename Bus>
167	inline void pb_v_data_sweep(Bus& bus, uint64_t scratch_gpa, uint64_t stride,
168	                            uint64_t vlenb, bool load)
169	{
170	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(5), vlenb);       // AVL
171	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(6), kVtypeE8M1);  // e8, m1, ta, ma
172	    const std::array<uint32_t, 1> pb_vsetvl = { encode_vsetvl(0, 5, 6) };
173	    exec_progbuf(bus, std::span<const uint32_t>{pb_vsetvl});
174	
175	    // vle8.v/vse8.v are register-indirect with no immediate offset, so the base
176	    // pointer x7 must step one register-span between transfers. Advance it with
177	    // an `addi` INSIDE the Program Buffer and pack as many (transfer; addi)
178	    // pairs as fit (kProgbufMaxInsns / 2 = 7) into each execution. Each PB
179	    // execution is one halted-hart DM round-trip (~1000 sim cycles spent in the
180	    // busy-poll), so the cost is the NUMBER of executions: batching cuts 32
181	    // registers from 32 executions + 32 per-register x7 writes down to
182	    // ceil(32/7) = 5 executions and ONE x7 write. x7 persists across executions
183	    // (the hart stays halted), so each batch resumes advancing where the last
184	    // one stopped.
185	    if (stride > 2047)  // addi imm12 is signed 12-bit; the wire span is 128
186	        throw std::runtime_error(
187	            "pb_v_data_sweep: register stride exceeds the addi imm12 range");
188	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(7), scratch_gpa);  // base, set once
189	
190	    constexpr std::size_t kRegsPerBatch = kProgbufMaxInsns / 2;  // 7
191	    const uint32_t addi_step = encode_addi(7, 7, static_cast<int32_t>(stride));
192	    std::array<uint32_t, kRegsPerBatch * 2> batch{};
193	    std::size_t n = 0;
194	    for (uint16_t i = 0; i < 32; ++i) {
195	        batch[n++] = load ? encode_vle8_v(static_cast<uint8_t>(i), 7)
196	                          : encode_vse8_v(static_cast<uint8_t>(i), 7);
197	        batch[n++] = addi_step;
198	        if (n == batch.size() || i == 31) {
199	            exec_progbuf(bus, std::span<const uint32_t>{batch.data(), n});
200	            n = 0;
201	        }
202	    }
203	}
204	
205	}  // namespace hybrid
206

## Simplification Review - Findings

**File: src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp, lines 194-202 (batching loop)**

**Issue:** The batching loop uses a running index `n` with a dual flush-condition (`n == batch.size() || i == 31`). The last-register condition `i == 31` exists because the trailing addi after v31 is dead work—it advances x7 past the end, but x7 is never used again. This makes the condition redundant with the logic.

**Simpler form:** Standard chunked loop without the explicit `i == 31` guard. Use `std::min()` to compute the actual batch size on the final iteration:
```cpp
constexpr std::size_t batch_size = kRegsPerBatch * 2;
std::array<uint32_t, batch_size> batch{};
for (std::size_t idx = 0; idx < 32; ++idx) {
    const std::size_t batch_pos = (idx % kRegsPerBatch) * 2;
    batch[batch_pos]     = load ? encode_vle8_v(...) : encode_vse8_v(...);
    batch[batch_pos + 1] = addi_step;
    if (idx % kRegsPerBatch == kRegsPerBatch - 1 || idx == 31) {
        const std::size_t len = std::min(batch_size, (idx + 1 - (idx % kRegsPerBatch)) * 2);
        exec_progbuf(bus, std::span<const uint32_t>{batch.data(), len});
    }
}
```
Or simpler: just always flush when batch is full OR on final iteration; accept the dead addi as acceptable implementation detail (and add a comment explaining why).

**Cost:** Current design requires reader to reason about why the `i == 31` gate is needed. The dead work is not inherently problematic—just needs explicit documentation.

---

**File: tests/hybrid/program_buffer.test.cpp, lines 275–288**

**Issue:** `first_x7_is_base` duplicates verification logic already proven by earlier assertions:
- `CHECK(count_x7_abstract_writes(bus) == 1)` proves exactly ONE x7 write occurs
- `CHECK(progbuf_holds(bus, encode_addi(...)))` proves the addi is in the buffer

The `first_x7_is_base` block re-scans the write sequence to verify the single x7 command is preceded by data0/data1 staging the scratch base. This is redundant—if `count_x7_abstract_writes == 1` and the batching loop only writes x7 once (at the start with `scratch_gpa`), the assertion is over-specified.

**Simpler form:** Remove the 14-line `first_x7_is_base` block entirely. It re-derives what `count_x7_abstract_writes(bus) == 1` + knowledge of the code already proves. The test confirms:
1. Exactly one x7 write → it must be the base (no per-register writes)
2. The write happens → staging is correct by construction

**Cost:** ~14 lines of redundant scanning logic; saves reader complexity.

---

**File: tests/hybrid/program_buffer.test.cpp, resume_driver.test.cpp, state_drain.test.cpp**

**Issue:** Three separate implementations of "scan progbuf slots for an instruction":
- `program_buffer.test.cpp:248-254`: `progbuf_holds(bus, insn)` (free function)
- `resume_driver.test.cpp:954-959`: `in_progbuf` lambda (local inline)
- `state_drain.test.cpp:480-486`: inlined 4-line range check (no helper)

All three check: `reg >= kProgbuf0 && reg <= kProgbuf0 + kProgbufMaxInsns && value == insn`.

**Simpler form:** Extract `progbuf_holds` (or `in_progbuf`) to a shared test utility header or namespace, then use it uniformly in all three files. Eliminates duplication and improves maintainability.

**Cost:** 3 redundant implementations of identical logic; potential drift if one is updated without the others.

---

**File: tests/hybrid/resume_driver.test.cpp, lines 954–959**

**Issue:** The lambda `in_progbuf` is defined but used in only one test case. It's nearly identical to the standalone `progbuf_holds` helper in program_buffer.test.cpp (same 5-line logic).

**Simpler form:** Use the shared `progbuf_holds` from program_buffer.test.cpp or move the lambda to a common test namespace and reuse.

**Cost:** Redundant definition; makes future updates error-prone.

---

## Summary

| File | Line(s) | Issue | Simpler Form | Cost |
|------|---------|-------|-------------|------|
| `src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp` | 194–202 | Batching loop with dual flush condition (`n == batch.size() \|\| i == 31`) — dead addi after v31 makes second gate subtle | Document the dead addi as acceptable, or switch to standard chunked-loop pattern | Needs 1-line comment explaining why trailing addi is dead work |
| `tests/hybrid/program_buffer.test.cpp` | 275–288 | `first_x7_is_base` re-derives what `count_x7_abstract_writes(bus) == 1` already proves | Remove entirely; the single x7 write must be the base by construction | Delete 14-line block |
| `tests/hybrid/{program_buffer,resume_driver,state_drain}.test.cpp` | various | Three identical "scan progbuf slots" implementations (free function, lambda, inlined) | Extract `progbuf_holds` to shared test utility; import in all 3 files | Consolidate 3 implementations into 1 |

**Overall: Code is clean. The main opportunities are (1) clarify the dead addi with a comment, (2) drop over-specified `first_x7_is_base` assertion, (3) deduplicate the progbuf-scan logic across test files.**
